idiom_name: Jakarta REST (JAX-RS) resource classes + generated OpenAPI document
implementation_notes: Jakarta REST is the standard publication mechanism: a resource class annotated @Path("/v1/orders") is the host service, @Consumes/@Produces pin the representation, and the mapping from domain model to DTO records is an explicit facade, so JPA entities and aggregates never cross the boundary. The contract document comes from the annotations - MicroProfile OpenAPI or springdoc turn the resource classes into the OpenAPI document consumers read - and the version is carried either in the path or in a vendor media type (@Produces("application/vnd.acme.v1+json")), which keeps one path serving several versions. The framework replaces the wiring (routing, content negotiation, serialisation, document generation) but not the decisions: which capabilities become published services and what the deprecation policy is stay with the host team.
pitfalls: Returning JPA entities from resource methods serialises lazy proxies and persistence internals onto the wire; expose DTOs only.
Framework defaults (XML negotiation, Jackson field naming, null handling) sneak into the published contract unless the media type and mapper configuration are pinned explicitly.
OpenAPI generation reflects the annotations only: missing @Schema/@Parameter/@APIResponse descriptions produce a technically valid but undocumented - and therefore unusable - contract.
